subject: How naming variables change lavaan behavior?

messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: How naming variables change lavaan behavior?
parts:
Hello all,

Can anyone explain me why I have to comment the following lines below in my model below for it to converge?

#y2w1 ~~ var1*y2w1 + 0*y2w2 + 0*y2w3
#y2w2 ~~ var2*y2w2 + 0*y2w3
#y2w3 ~~ var3*y2w3


If these three lines are commented out, I get a perfect fit. 

> fitMeasures(mod2ind3lv1.fit)[c("df",'tli',"cfi","rmsea")]
   df   tli   cfi rmsea
    0     1     1     0 

If the lines are added to the model, I get the following warning and an error when asking for fit statistics. I just wanted to name the variables to refer to them later, was not planning to add restrictions or anything.  I was expecting lavaan to estimate the vars and report back. Why naming variables changes software behavior? How does it change? 


Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel2, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= 2.265979e-20) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the
    model is not identified.
> fitMeasures(mod2ind3lv1.fit)[c("df",'tli',"cfi","rmsea")]
Error in TEST[[2]] : subscript out of bounds

Best regards,

Hugo

------------------------------------------------------



mod2ind3lv1.indicator_effects.delta_conditional <- '

lv1 =~ l1*y2w1 + l2*y2w2 + l3*y2w3
l1 + l2 + l3 == 3

lv1 ~ lv1mean*1
lv1 ~~ lv1var*lv1

## LIR means
y2w1 ~ int1*1
y2w2 ~ int2*1
y2w3 ~ int3*1
int1==0
int2==0
int3==0

## thresholds link LIRs to observed items
y2w1 | thr1*t1
y2w2 | thr2*t1
y2w3 | thr3*t1
thr1 + thr2 +thr3 ==0

## LIR (co)variances
#y2w1 ~~ var1*y2w1 + 0*y2w2 + 0*y2w3     # problematic lines
#y2w2 ~~ var2*y2w2 + 0*y2w3                     # problematic lines
#y2w3 ~~ var3*y2w3                                     # problematic lines
'

sem.model <- mod2ind3lv1.indicator_effects.delta_conditional
rm(mod2ind3lv1.fit)
mod2ind3lv1.fit <- lavaan(model = sem.model,
                          data = dat,
                          std.lv = FALSE,
                          int.ov.free = TRUE,
                          int.lv.free = TRUE,
                          meanstructure =TRUE,
                          auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                          auto.var = TRUE,
                          auto.th = TRUE,
                          ordered = c("y2w1","y2w2","y2w3"),
                          parameterization = "delta")
summary(mod2ind3lv1.fit)
fitMeasures(mod2ind3lv1.fit)[c("df",'tli',"cfi","rmsea")]

messages.subject: Re: How naming variables change lavaan behavior?
parts: Can anyone explain me why I have to comment the following lines below in my model below for it to converge?

Because those items are categorical, so their variances are not identified (unless you place very strange, arbitrary constraints on their intercepts and thresholds).

Can anyone explain me why I have to comment the following lines below in my model below for it to converge?

Because those items are categorical, so their variances are not identified (unless you place very strange, arbitrary constraints on their intercepts and thresholds).

if(!require(MASS)) install.packages("MASS"); library(MASS)
if(!require(rockchalk)) install.packages("rockchalk"); library(rockchalk)
if(!require(lavaan)) install.packages("lavaan"); library(lavaan)


# Generate Longitudinal Items from a Bivariate LIR
data_creation <-function(){}

N <- 2000 ## subjects
I= 3  # Number of Items
PL=2 # Logistic Model (1,2,3 parameters)
SigmaType <- 3 # 0 = Covariance Uniform, 1 = Covariancia AR1, 2 =  Covariancia de bandas 3 = Covariancia Nula
rho<-0.7

coefs <- matrix(ncol=6,nrow=I)
colnames(coefs)=c("a1","b1","c1","a2","b2","c2")

if (PL==1) {a = rep(1,I)} else {a = runif(I,0.5, 2.5)}    # U(0.5 , 2.5)
b = runif(I,-2, 2.0)     # U(-2 , 2)
if (PL<=2) {c = rep(0,I)} else{c = runif(I,0.0, 0.3) } # U(0 , 0.3)

d=-a*b # MIRT trabalha com o intercepto (d=-ab) e nao com a dificuldade (b)

if(SigmaType==0){
  Sigma <- lazyCor(c(rho,rho,rho)) #Matriz de Covariancia Uniforme
}else if(SigmaType==1){
  Sigma <- lazyCor(c(rho,rho*rho,rho)) #Matriz de Covariancia AR(1)
}else if(SigmaType==2){
  Sigma <- lazyCor(c(rho,0,0)) #Matriz de Covariancia de bandas
}else if(SigmaType==3){
  Sigma <- lazyCor(c(0,0,0)) #Matriz de Covariancia nula
}else{
  Sigma <- NULL
}
Sigma

Theta <- mvrnorm(n=N, mu=c(0,0.5,1), Sigma )



dat =simdata(a=a,d=d,N=N,itemtype = '2PL', Theta = matrix(Theta[,1],ncol=1,nrow = length(Theta[,1])))
colnames(dat) <-    c("y2w1","y2w2","y2w3")

prop <- colSums(dat)/nrow(dat)
th <- qnorm(1-prop)
th #expected thresholds

lv1 =~ l1*y2w1 + l2*y2w2 + l3*y2w3
l1 + l2 + l3 == 3

lv1 ~ lv1mean*1
lv1 ~~ lv1var*lv1

## LIR means
y2w1 ~ int1*1
y2w2 ~ int2*1
y2w3 ~ int3*1

int1+int2+int3==0

int1 + l1*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint
int2 + l2*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint
int3 + l3*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint

## thresholds link LIRs to observed items
y2w1 | thr1*t1
y2w2 | thr2*t1
y2w3 | thr3*t1
## LIR (co)variances
y2w1 ~~ var1*y2w1 + 0*y2w2 + 0*y2w3     # problematic lines
y2w2 ~~ var2*y2w2 + 0*y2w3                     # problematic lines
y2w3 ~~ var3*y2w3                                     # problematic lines

lv1var*l1^2 + var1 == 1 # delta parameterization <- new constraint
lv1var*l2^2 + var2 == 1 # delta parameterization <- new constraint
lv1var*l3^2 + var3 == 1 # delta parameterization <- new constraint

'

mod2ind3lv1.indicator_effects.theta_marginal <- '

lv1 =~ l1*y2w1 + l2*y2w2 + l3*y2w3
l1 + l2 + l3 == 3

lv1 ~ lv1mean*1
lv1 ~~ lv1var*lv1

## LIR means
y2w1 ~ int1*1
y2w2 ~ int2*1
y2w3 ~ int3*1

int1+int2+int3==0

int1 + l1*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint  
int2 + l2*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint  
int3 + l3*lv1mean ==0 #<- new constraint

## thresholds link LIRs to observed items
y2w1 | thr1*t1
y2w2 | thr2*t1
y2w3 | thr3*t1
## LIR (co)variances
y2w1 ~~ var1*y2w1 + 0*y2w2 + 0*y2w3     # problematic lines
y2w2 ~~ var2*y2w2 + 0*y2w3                     # problematic lines
y2w3 ~~ var3*y2w3                                     # problematic lines

var1==1 #theta parameterization <- new constraint  
var2==1 #theta parameterization <- new constraint  
var3==1 #theta parameterization <- new constraint  

'
theta <-TRUE
if(theta==TRUE){
  sem.model <- mod2ind3lv1.indicator_effects.theta_marginal
}else{

sem.model <- mod2ind3lv1.indicator_effects.delta_conditional

messages.subject: Re: How naming variables change lavaan behavior?
parts: What I really think it is strange is that I had code into mymodel  the theta/delta parameterizatons to make lavaan work with the respective parameterizations. Is that expected?

Only because you are trying to override default behavior by estimating the intercepts.

Or am I overdoing?

Maybe.  Not sure why you want to constrain the marginal expectations of latent item-responses to be zero, even in the theta parameterization (in which the conditional rather than marginal variances are constrained to 1) instead of the conditional expectations (i.e., intercepts).  But if that is meaningful to you, perhaps to make it equivalent to some IRT model (you seem to be using mirt along with lavaan), then you are free to define whatever model you want, within the capabilities of the software.  Going beyond the software's defaults will always require more effort on your part, by definition.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How naming variables change lavaan behavior?
parts: I am trying to define the mean and var of the LIR so that threshold can be correctly calculated LIR ~ N(0,1) as per your presentation.

Then why are you trying to estimate the common-factor mean?  It is ultimately an arbitrary location, so it is much simpler if you just let it remain fixed to zero for identification.  That way, the conditional LIR means (i.e., intercepts) are already interpreted as the means when the common-factor == its mean (because it is zero).  Then you don't need to break your back trying to correctly define the parameters needed for your identification constraints; lavaan's default constraints will already do that (assuming you use cfa() or set the same lavOptions that cfa() does).

When you get to your longitudinal model, you simply need to specify invariance constraints across time, which allow the common-factor mean to be estimated at Time 2.  Because the common-factor's mean at Time 1 is fixed to zero, the Time-2 mean can already be interpreted as the change from Time 1.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
